nodes.label: ADR-0001 Vertical slice architecture
nodes.rationale: Layering would split a withdrawal's read-modify-write across four projects, hiding the race the repo exists to show; IAccountRepository.Update looks identical for a blind overwrite and a version-checked update. Modular monolith solves a team-boundary problem this single-context repo does not have. Accepted costs: no compile-time dependency enforcement, deliberate duplication between slices, and unfamiliarity to reviewers who expect Clean architecture.

nodes.label: ADR-0002 Plain handler classes, no MediatR
nodes.rationale: MediatR is commercially licensed and a public teaching repo should not carry a paid dependency; more importantly its pipeline hides the exact lines that race. A hand-rolled dispatcher would reproduce the indirection without the ecosystem — worst of both. Costs accepted: no pipeline behaviours, endpoints depend on concrete handler types, scales badly past a few dozen handlers.

nodes.label: NaiveWithdrawHandler (deliberately lossy)
nodes.rationale: Performs an unguarded read-decide-write and is supposed to lose updates; tests assert that it does. Fixing it removes the lesson.

nodes.label: InMemoryAccountStore (unsafe singleton on purpose)
nodes.rationale: Deliberately not thread-safe at the account level and registered as a singleton. Adding a lock or scoping it per-request silently deletes the bug the repo is built to demonstrate.

nodes.label: ScaleEndpoints sync-over-async endpoint
nodes.rationale: Calls .GetAwaiter().GetResult() on purpose to demonstrate thread-pool starvation under load.

nodes.label: InterestStrategies ParallelWithLock / ParallelWithConcurrentQueue
nodes.rationale: Slow on purpose — the 'I parallelised it and it got slower' result.

nodes.label: Warnings are errors (CS9113)
nodes.rationale: TreatWarningsAsErrors in Directory.Build.props turns an unread primary-constructor parameter into a build failure; use the parameter or drop it.

nodes.label: No commercially-licensed dependencies
nodes.rationale: MediatR, FluentAssertions and NBomber rejected on licence grounds so a reader can use the same approach at work; Shouldly and an in-repo load harness replace them.

nodes.label: Gate before acquiring a lock
nodes.rationale: Gating inside a critical section deadlocks: the lock holder waits at a barrier for actors who cannot enter until it releases.

nodes.label: Only the first retry attempt joins the barrier
nodes.rationale: Retrying actors that re-join a barrier stall the run until the 5s timeout, because actors that already finished never arrive.

nodes.label: Fresh DbContext per retry attempt
nodes.rationale: Reusing one keeps the stale entity in the change tracker, so the retry re-sends the same doomed UPDATE forever.

nodes.label: xmin is a PostgreSQL system column
nodes.rationale: Not included in SELECT *, so raw SQL must say SELECT *, xmin FROM "Accounts" or EF fails to materialise the entity.

nodes.label: DbContext is not thread-safe
nodes.rationale: Concurrent actors each need their own context from IDbContextFactory<BankDbContext>.

nodes.label: Money is decimal, cents are long
No Docker daemon in this environment
nodes.rationale: The 3-replica demo has only ever been `docker compose config`-validated; claiming it was run would be false.

nodes.label: IWithdrawStrategy
nodes.rationale: Must be registered as a singleton in Program.cs — an unregistered strategy compiles and silently never appears in /api/lab/strategies.

nodes.label: IContentionRecorder
nodes.rationale: Called from inside the code under observation, so it must never block, do I/O or throw; use Interlocked for counters and push SignalR fan-out to the background ContentionBroadcaster.

nodes.label: IAccountLock
nodes.rationale: Two implementations behind one interface; swapping the DI registration is the entire scale-out lesson.

nodes.label: InProcessAccountLock
nodes.rationale: Correct on one instance only — process memory is not shared between replicas.

nodes.label: PostgresAdvisoryAccountLock
nodes.rationale: Survives any number of instances because the coordination point is the database.

nodes.label: Gate placement rule
nodes.rationale: Lock-taking handlers gate at BeforeAcquire, lock-free handlers at AfterRead; the 5-second gate cap is a safety net, not a licence to gate in the wrong place.

nodes.label: RunSummaryCalculator
nodes.rationale: Every verdict — who won, who lost silently, whether money was conserved — is computed server-side here and tested; the UI must not recompute or second-guess it.

nodes.label: Signals, no NgRx
nodes.rationale: The UI is a presentation surface; a state library would add ceremony that teaches nothing about concurrency.

nodes.label: CORS must allow localhost and 127.0.0.1
nodes.rationale: A browser treats them as different origins, so allowing one makes every call fail as if the API were down; a wildcard origin is impossible because SignalR needs AllowCredentials.

nodes.label: SignalR groups are per-process
nodes.rationale: Behind more than one replica this needs a Redis backplane; without one clients silently miss events, so the live feed is an accelerator and the REST timeline stays the source of truth.

nodes.label: Never assert an ordering you did not force
nodes.rationale: Asserting a specific actor won is asserting the scheduler's mood and will fail eventually; assert only what holds under every interleaving.

nodes.label: Relative-only timing assertions
nodes.rationale: Absolute upper bounds flake on a loaded machine; absolute lower bounds derived from the work are fine. Two performance-ratio assertions were deleted in M5 after failing under CPU load — ratios belong in BenchmarkDotNet, which has warmup and error bars.

nodes.label: TimingSensitiveCollection
nodes.rationale: Disables parallelisation so an elapsed-time test is not competing with three others for the same cores.

nodes.label: Three-tier test strategy
nodes.rationale: Deterministic tests may assert a specific forced interleaving; invariant tests assert only what holds under every interleaving; integration tests against real PostgreSQL are the only place concurrency tokens and row locks are real.

nodes.label: InvariantSuiteHasTeethTests
nodes.rationale: Points the invariants at the naive handler and requires them to fail; if they start passing the suite has stopped applying pressure.

nodes.label: No EF Core in-memory provider for integration tests
nodes.rationale: It implements neither concurrency tokens nor row locks, so tests would pass against a system that is still broken.

nodes.label: ADR template with mandatory sections
nodes.rationale: Why not the others, Trade-offs accepted and Interview angle are mandatory and hook-checked: a decision you cannot argue against is a default you inherited, and an ADR with no downside listed is a rationalisation.

nodes.label: Every measured claim must be real
nodes.rationale: A benchmark whose conditions you cannot state is a number, not evidence; figures came from a 4-core shared VM under a ShortRun job with wide error bars.

nodes.label: IInterleaveGate seam
nodes.rationale: A testability hook deliberately placed on the production hot path: NoOpInterleaveGate in production, ScriptedInterleaveGate in tests, making the lost update 100% reproducible instead of a race test that hopes for a collision.

nodes.label: Concurrency vs parallelism mental model
nodes.rationale: One teller juggling many customers (interleaved, async over I/O) versus many tellers at many counters (simultaneous, needs cores).

nodes.label: Optimistic vs pessimistic concurrency
nodes.rationale: Contention rate is the deciding variable: rare collisions favour detect-and-retry, common collisions on hot rows favour queue-and-wait; long user think time forbids holding a DB lock.

nodes.label: Scaling as three layers
nodes.rationale: Application code (how it waits), instances (Kubernetes multiplies instances but cannot fix code sharing mutable process memory), then data (row contention, not CPU, is the wall).

nodes.label: Silent losers in RunSummary
nodes.rationale: Actors whose write was overwritten and who were told they succeeded — the punchline of the whole lab.

nodes.label: .NET 8 LTS forced by blocked CDN
nodes.rationale: builds.dotnet.microsoft.com is proxy-blocked (403), so dotnet-install.sh fails and .NET 9/10 cannot be obtained in this environment.

nodes.label: Thread-pool starvation result (979 vs 35 RPS)
nodes.rationale: One .Result instead of await collapses throughput from 979 to 35 RPS and p99 from 105 ms to 3531 ms on identical hardware.

nodes.label: In-process lock breaks across three replicas
nodes.rationale: No application code changes between the two compose files; only process memory stops being shared, which is enough to break every strategy whose coordination lives in process memory while optimistic, pessimistic and advisory-lock strategies keep working.

hyperedges.label: Deliberate defects that must stay broken
Adding a concurrency slice end to end
Making a race deterministic without flaky tests
